title: Existing-Home Sales (NAR, September 2026 data) — the unscheduled solo vintage a live sibling kill switch is keyed to, and nothing was due to look, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: nar.realtor/press-releases/nar-statistical-news-release-schedule, fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 483,177 bytes), whose 2026 table reads verbatim "OCTOBER | Tue., Oct. 13 | September Existing-Home Sales" under the page's standing note "All releases at 10 a.m. Eastern Time", and its downloadable twin /sites/default/files/2025-11/2026-nar-statistical-news-release-schedule.docx (HTTP 200, 55,384 bytes, published 2025-11), unzipped and read as XML, which carries the identical October row. Filed `estimate` rather than `confirmed` on the one count that is not date doubt: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the same limit existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 and existing-home-sales-2026-09-10 both recorded before their own initial research promoted them on this identical page. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the existing-home-sales-2026-09-10 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08, D-2). PROPOSED OVER A SIBLING'S ON-RECORD DECLINE, and the reason is mechanical rather than a difference of taste. existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 declined this edition on 2026-09-06 as "a routine monthly edition… the thing worth watching is a workbook re-pull at the next pulse, not a calendar row" — while in the same document making 2026-10-13 the dated observation for its own first kill switch: "No `ContribArchives` vintage dated 2026-10-13 exists by 2026-10-16… Its absence would mean the premise Leg 2 refutes is right after all, a month before it matters." Those two statements do not survive together on that ledger's own cadence. 11-12 is `low` impact, so assessment-cadence.json puts it in the `15+` band at every 30 days: its next pulse is 2026-10-06 (37 days out, still the 15+ band) and the one after that is 2026-11-05. The 2026-10-16 deadline falls in the 30-day gap between them, so the kill switch's observation date is unreachable on the schedule its own lane set, and event-scan.mjs surfaces nothing on 10-13 or 10-16 because no calendar entry exists. A `never-assessed` row here is what makes the rehearsal actually get looked at. The edition is also distinguishable on its own evidence, re-derived this session: the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (fetched direct 2026-09-08) schedules NO posting on 2026-10-13 and names existing-home sales on only four 2026 dates (01-14, 06-09, 09-10, 12-09), so 10-13 carries the unscheduled shape that produced a SOLO vintage on all five of 2026's unscheduled EHS dates so far (02-12, 03-10, 04-13, 05-11, 07-09) — the same shape 11-12 predicts for itself, arriving a month earlier and free. Impact `low` and symbols empty, adopting rather than re-deriving the tape measurement this lane ran on 2,514 daily sessions 2016-09-06 -> 2026-09-04: 114 EHS release days leave ITB (p=0.57), XHB (p=0.46) and SPY (p=0.65) at baseline, and the 100 solo-vintage ones do too (ITB 1.915% vs 1.869%, p=0.63). An inert tape, and nothing here licenses an entry. Unlike its 09-10 sibling this edition sits OUTSIDE any FOMC blackout — the 2026-10-28 meeting's window opens 2026-10-17 — which matters because blackout sessions are the measured widener for homebuilders (ITB 2.003% vs 1.838%, p<0.001, n=678), not the print. Proposed as an estimate; estimates widen caution, never trigger action.
